subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Hadith of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) as a Model of Good Character
overview: Allah sent Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) to teach people the best manners. In this sub-strand you will read his Hadith on good character, study how he was trustworthy, truthful, kind and generous, and practise those traits at home and at school.

lessons.title: The Hadith on perfecting good character
objectives: Read the selected Hadith on the character of the Prophet (S.A.W.).
Give the meaning of the Hadith in simple words.
Explain why good character is part of his message.
lessons.intro: People sometimes think religion is only prayer and fasting. The Prophet (S.A.W.) showed that how we treat people is part of the message he was sent with. A short Hadith states that purpose clearly.
lessons.notes:
### The selected Hadith
The Prophet (S.A.W.) said: “I have been sent for the purpose of perfecting good morals.” This Hadith is narrated by Al-Hakim. Morals, or akhlaq, are the manners and character a person lives by: truth, trust, kindness, patience and fairness.

### What the words mean
“I have been sent” means Allah sent him as a messenger. “Perfecting good morals” means completing and teaching the best character, so that people reach the highest standard of behaviour. He did not come only to recite words. He came to build people whose actions match those words.

### Why this Hadith matters
A Muslim can pray and still hurt classmates with lies, insults or selfishness. That person has missed a main part of the Prophet’s mission. The Qur’an describes the Prophet (S.A.W.) as being upon a great character. His companions learned Islam by watching how he spoke, how he forgave and how he kept a trust.

Reading the Hadith correctly is the first step. Say it slowly, write it in your notebook, and be ready to explain it without changing the meaning. When someone asks what the Prophet was sent to do, you can answer with this Hadith: he was sent to perfect good character. The lessons that follow will name four of those character traits and show how a Grade 4 learner copies them.

keyWords.meaning: a saying, action or approval of the Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)
the rules of good behaviour a person lives by

examples.problem: A learner says, “I pray, so my habit of lying does not matter.” How does this Hadith answer him?
steps: The Prophet (S.A.W.) was sent to perfect good morals.
Telling the truth is part of good character.
Prayer and good character belong together.
examples.answer: Lying goes against the purpose of the Prophet’s message. Prayer should be joined with truthful character.

activity.title: Read and explain the Hadith
materials: The Hadith written on the board or on a card
steps: Read aloud, as a class: “I have been sent for the purpose of perfecting good morals.”
Each learner reads it again, clearly, to a partner.
In pairs, explain the meaning in your own words without adding ideas that are not in the Hadith.
Write the Hadith and its meaning in your notebook, and name the narrator as Al-Hakim.

practice.question: Write the selected Hadith on the character of the Prophet (S.A.W.).
practice.answer: “I have been sent for the purpose of perfecting good morals.”

practice.question: Who narrated this Hadith, according to the curriculum text?
What does ‘perfecting good morals’ mean?
practice.answer: Completing and teaching the best manners and character.

summary: The Prophet (S.A.W.) said he was sent to perfect good morals.
The Hadith is narrated by Al-Hakim.
Good character is part of his message, together with worship.

lessons.title: Trustworthy, truthful, kind and generous
objectives: Describe four character traits of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.).
Tell how he was known as Al-Amin before prophethood.
Give an example of each trait from his life.
lessons.intro: Long before the Qur’an was revealed, the people of Makkah already had a name for the young Muhammad (S.A.W.). They called him Al-Amin, the Trustworthy, and As-Sadiq, the Truthful. Those names tell us what a good young person looks like.
lessons.notes:
### Four traits to study
The life of the Prophet (S.A.W.) shows many good traits. Four that every learner can copy are these:

- Trustworthy: people kept their goods with him because he did not betray a trust. He was known as Al-Amin.
- Truthful: he did not lie. He was known as As-Sadiq even by people who later opposed his message.
- Kind: he spoke gently, visited the sick, and did not crush the weak.
- Generous: he gave to people in need and did not love hoarding wealth.

### A story of trust
When the Quraysh were rebuilding the Ka’bah, the clans quarrelled over who would put the Black Stone back in its place. They agreed that the first person to enter would decide. Muhammad (S.A.W.) entered, and they were pleased because he was Al-Amin. He placed the stone on a cloth and asked each clan to hold a corner, so they raised it together. Then he set the stone in place. He solved the quarrel without taking the honour for himself alone.

### As a youth
He was an orphan. His father died before he was born, and he lost his mother while he was still young. He worked, including as a shepherd, and people trusted him in trade. He did not worship the idols of Makkah. The question “What were his traits as a youth?” is answered by the names people already gave him: truthful and trustworthy, and by his kindness to those who had less power than he did.

A good child today tells the truth, returns what is borrowed, speaks kindly and shares. Those are the same traits, lived at school age.

keyWords.meaning: the Trustworthy, a name given to the Prophet (S.A.W.)
ready to give and to share

examples.problem: The clans in Makkah could have fought over the Black Stone. How did the Prophet’s trustworthiness prevent that?
steps: They accepted him as the judge because he was Al-Amin.
He let every clan share the honour by holding the cloth.
Nobody was cheated, and the stone was set in place.
examples.answer: They trusted his decision, and he shared the honour fairly among the clans.

activity.title: Listen to a story of the Prophet’s character
materials: A short story or video of the Black Stone, told by the teacher or played from a digital device
steps: Watch or listen quietly to the story of the Black Stone.
In groups, discuss how the story shows that he was trustworthy, and add one example each of truthfulness, kindness and generosity.
Write the four traits on manila paper with a school example under each.
Present the chart to the class and listen respectfully when other groups speak.

practice.question: What do the names Al-Amin and As-Sadiq mean?
practice.answer: Al-Amin means the Trustworthy, and As-Sadiq means the Truthful.

practice.question: How did the Prophet (S.A.W.) settle the quarrel about the Black Stone?
practice.answer: He placed it on a cloth so each clan could hold a corner, and then he set the stone in place.

practice.question: Name four character traits of the Prophet (S.A.W.) studied in this lesson.
Why did people accept him as the judge in the story of the Black Stone?
practice.answer: Because he was already known as Al-Amin, the Trustworthy.

summary: The Prophet (S.A.W.) was trustworthy, truthful, kind and generous.
People called him Al-Amin and As-Sadiq before prophethood.
The story of the Black Stone shows fairness and trust.

lessons.title: Copying the Prophet’s character every day
objectives: Role-play the traits of the Prophet (S.A.W.) in school situations.
Choose one trait to practise this week.
Explain why following his character honours him as a role model.
lessons.intro: Knowing that the Prophet (S.A.W.) was kind is not the same as being kind when a younger learner drops a set of books. This lesson turns the four traits into actions a learner can do today.
lessons.notes:
### A role model is copied
A role model is a person whose life we try to follow. Muslims take Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.) as the best role model because Allah sent him to perfect good morals, and because his own life matched his teaching. Valuing him means more than saying “Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam”. It means practising his traits when nobody is giving a prize.

### What emulation looks like at your age
- Trustworthy: return a borrowed pen, keep a secret that is not harmful, and do not open another person’s bag. If a teacher leaves you in charge of the class list, you do not change marks.
- Truthful: admit a mistake even when you may be corrected. Do not copy answers and call them your own. As-Sadiq did not lie to escape trouble.
- Kind: speak softly to a new learner, help someone who is hurt, and refuse to join in laughing at a classmate. Kindness includes animals and younger children.
- Generous: share a sharpener, explain a sum to a friend, or give a coin in charity from what a parent allows. Generosity is not only money. Time and knowledge can be given too.

### Making it a habit
Choose one trait for this week and tell a partner how you will show it. At the end of the week, check yourself honestly. If you fail, do not give up. The Prophet’s message is to keep growing in character. When you practise these traits you are answering the Hadith with your actions, and you are showing that you value him as your model.

keyWords.meaning: a person whose good life we try to copy
to copy someone’s good behaviour in your own life

examples.problem: You find a classmate’s fifty-shilling note on the floor and nobody is looking. Which trait of the Prophet guides you, and what do you do?
steps: Al-Amin returned trusts and did not take what was not his.
The note belongs to the classmate.
Hand it to the classmate or to the teacher.
examples.answer: Trustworthiness. Give the money back to the owner or to the teacher.

activity.title: Role-play the four traits
materials: Four situation cards: a lost pen, a broken window, a crying younger child, a friend without a pencil
steps: In groups, pick one situation card.
Act two short scenes: one in which the learner ignores the Prophet’s character, and one in which the learner copies it.
The class names the trait they saw: trustworthy, truthful, kind or generous.
Each learner writes one trait he or she will practise this week and how it will be done.

practice.question: What does it mean to emulate the Prophet (S.A.W.)?
practice.answer: To copy his good character in one’s own daily life.

practice.question: Give one school action that shows truthfulness.
practice.answer: Any one: admit a mistake, do not cheat in a test, tell the teacher what really happened.

practice.question: Generosity is not only money. Give one other way to be generous.
practice.answer: Share knowledge, time or learning materials, such as explaining work or lending a pencil.

practice.question: Why is practising his character a way of valuing him?
practice.answer: Because he was sent to perfect good morals, so following those morals honours his message.

summary: A Muslim copies the Prophet (S.A.W.) in trust, truth, kindness and generosity.
School life gives daily chances to practise each trait.
Valuing him means living his character, not only praising him.

quiz.question: Complete the Hadith: “I have been sent for the purpose of …”
quiz.explanation: The selected Hadith, narrated by Al-Hakim, says he was sent to perfect good morals.

quiz.question: Who is named as the narrator of this Hadith in the Grade 4 design?
quiz.explanation: The curriculum text says the Hadith is narrated by Al-Hakim.

quiz.question: What does Al-Amin mean?
quiz.explanation: People of Makkah called him Al-Amin because they trusted him.

quiz.question: What does As-Sadiq mean?
quiz.explanation: As-Sadiq is the name that points to his truthfulness.

quiz.question: In the story of the Black Stone, why were the clans pleased when he entered?
options: He was known as the Trustworthy
quiz.explanation: They accepted Al-Amin as the one who should decide.

quiz.question: How did he let all the clans share the honour of raising the Black Stone?
quiz.answer: He placed the stone on a cloth and each clan held a corner.
quiz.explanation: Then he set the stone in its place. The plan was fair to every clan.

quiz.question: You break a class ruler by mistake. Which trait tells you to admit it?
quiz.explanation: As-Sadiq did not hide the truth to escape trouble.

quiz.question: Which action emulates his generosity at school?
options: Explaining a lesson to a friend who is stuck
quiz.explanation: Generosity includes sharing knowledge and help, not only money.

quiz.question: A good child in Islam is best described as a learner who…
options: is truthful, trustworthy, kind and generous
quiz.explanation: These are the character traits studied from the Prophet’s example.

quiz.question: Why do Muslims take the Prophet (S.A.W.) as their role model of character?
quiz.answer: Allah sent him to perfect good morals, and his own life matched that teaching.
quiz.explanation: Valuing him means practising those traits in daily life.
